rules.description: The compositor is the only product entry into the resolved-material graph executor.
The composition helper is the only runtime call into the claimed submission coordinator.
Legacy planner calls still reachable from product planning are frozen until each family migrates.
The retired legacy planner must not regain diagnostic or static-disposition observation authority.
All external legacy planner references are frozen so a new product or observation owner cannot appear in another file.
Direct main-pass encoder writers remain explicit while object and utility paths migrate to the frame scheduler.
Product source must not reconstruct or execute partial authored graphs through Iris, X-Ray, Cursor Ripple, or Shine recovery surfaces.
Expected SHA literals remain an explicit migration inventory and cannot increase.
Numeric Workshop paths are frozen until source profiles become public typed capabilities.
Named Workshop runtime profile dispatch is frozen until generic source contracts replace it.
The retired effect-chain owner, planner, catalog and compositor sentinel must never return to Scene product code.
Resolved capability admission must stop consulting a legacy backend yield decision before R4 completes.
A quad without a resolved claim must not recover a Light Shafts plan and write the main pass after R4 completes.
Retired fixed script compilers and verified-profile dispatch must not return anywhere in product Swift; public typed provider identities are not product owners.
The retired fixed SceneScript Audio Bars runtime owner must not be reintroduced anywhere in Scene product code.
The retired independent Image Blend plan and runtime owner must not be reintroduced anywhere in Scene product code.
The unified executor must not regain a whole-chain renderer or standalone effect-chain entry.
The product compositor must stop invoking the legacy authored whole-chain renderer before R4 completes.
R5 removes the legacy whole-chain compositor helper after its R4 product call is gone.
R5 removes the old whole-chain renderer call surface after GraphExecutor is the only product scheduler.
The retired dedicated stage renderer must not re-enter product execution.
R5 removes the legacy shader fallback graph definition and call after full graph preparation owns the path.
R5 removes legacyContract provenance after the fallback graph is unreachable.
R5 removes the old authored-effect telemetry owner after all legacy product routes are gone.
R5 removes the unreachable standalone authored renderer call surface.
R5 removes the unreachable single-stage legacy frame-plan surface.
R5 removes the old authored-chain frame-batch allocation and registration surface.
The base layer shader must remain a neutral source/dependency compositor and must not regain inline effect execution flags or parameter slots.
Effect resources must be resolved by typed descriptor identity rather than shared masks or path-fragment guessing.
Render targets must be prepared and committed through the persistent graph transaction; standalone direct pool allocation APIs must not return.
Scene product behavior must be selected from typed authored contracts, never from sample, wallpaper or Workshop item identifiers.
Source-shape analyzer types are the E5 semantic-derivation inventory and cannot grow; retirement shrinks this baseline family by family.
Product call sites of the bounded Swift shader frontend are frozen until the E5 fallback audit retires that frontend; direction is shrink to zero.
The legacy singular dependency route stays frozen until the E1 aggregate owner collapses it; direction is shrink to zero.
Scene product protocols require an explicit manifest ratchet with owner justification; accidental abstraction layers cannot appear.
